name: Week 15 KB Saturday Cardio — Conditioning (Spotlight: Brutal-Complex Finisher)
description: Saturday KB OPTION — pure conditioning, distinct from Tue (strength template) and Thu (lighter strength template). Light bell throughout (16-20lb working) — breathing rate and sustainability are the targets, not load. The Asgooch cardio complex + halo/figure-8-to-reverse-lunge flow combos carry over; the finisher block rotates this week from the controlled-power high-rep block to a light, high-rep BRUTAL-COMPLEX variant (swing / ab-stance goblet squat / alternating row / close-grip pushup). Choice-of-the-day on D6 alongside stairmaster, easy run, or rest.

dayOverview.theme: Saturday conditioning — light bell, more reps, more variety, breathing-rate target. Asgooch cardio complex + flow combos carry over; the finisher rotates to a light brutal-complex variant. Day after Friday legs — squatting stays LIGHT on purpose.

spotlights.why: The opening move of the rotated brutal-complex finisher, and the cleanest hinge-power drill on a light-bell day. Spotlight the hip-snap (hips drive the bell, NOT a squat, NOT an arm-lift) because under high-rep fatigue at the end of the session the swing is the first thing to turn into a squat-and-lift.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W14 controlled-power finisher · W15 brutal-complex-variant finisher (current) · W16 cycle forward — 100-rep block pull (from kb-100-rep-daily-challenge). The Asgooch cardio complex + flow combos stay; only the finisher block rotates so Saturday stays fresh.
watchpoints: **Day after Friday legs.** Squatting (front squat × 6 in the complex, the goblet/ab-stance squat in the finisher) stays LIGHT — 16-20lb. Skip the squat reps if the QL/quads are talking.
**Light bell is the whole point** — 16-20lb working. Conditioning means breathing rate, not bell weight.
**Asgooch CARDIO complex ≠ Tuesday's OVERHEAD complex** — same author, different chain. Cardio = row/clean/squat/snatch (low-and-explosive); overhead = row/snatch/OH lunge/OH squat/push press.
**Finisher rotated to a brutal-complex variant** — light bell, higher reps than the Tuesday version. It's conditioning, not a strength finisher; keep moving.
**Right shoulder watch on the snatch + the swing** — the punch-through / hip-snap is where the catch crashes. Light bell + smooth catch; if it crackles, drop to high pulls.
**Choice-of-the-day on D6** — not mandatory. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; swap for stairmaster / easy run if cardio-only is the call. No pull-up greasing here — Saturday is the conditioning flank.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Loosen the shoulders fast — the cardio complex is its own warmup.
Easy two-handed swings. Prime the hinge.
Light, open the hips. Skip if Friday legs left the quads sore.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Wakes the grip + forearm + posterior chain — primes the snatch catch.

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead.

sets.notes: **Abbreviated prep** — 4 moves instead of the full 7. Saturday is conditioning; the full template's 7-move prep is overkill for a light-bell day.

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — LEFT

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Left hand. Hips back, back flat, pull the elbow past the ribs. 2s pull, 2s lower.
Left hand. **Hip drive into the rack** — thumb to collarbone. Smooth catch — knees absorb.
Left rack. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Sit tall, full depth IF the legs are fresh; reduce depth before load if they're cooked.
Left hand. **Hips drive the bell**, not the arm — punch THROUGH at the top, smooth catch, no bang. Right shoulder watch on the catch — sub high pulls for the last 2 rounds if it crackles.

sets.notes: 5 rounds LEFT. Continuous within a round — row → clean → squat → snatch with no rest. Rest 30-45s between rounds. **Weak side first.** Different from Tuesday's overhead Asgooch — same author, different chain.

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — RIGHT

exercises.notes: Right hand. Same form — hips back, full extension.
Right hand. Smooth clean to the rack.
Right rack. Same depth/load discipline as the left.
Right hand. **Right shoulder watchpoint on the catch** — same modify-to-high-pull rule.

sets.notes: 5 rounds RIGHT. Continuous within a round. **If the workout is running long after the left side, drop to 3-4 rounds right — don't grind a quality session into a sloppy one.**

sets.name: Flow Combos — Halo/Figure-8 to Reverse Lunge

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Halo one direction → reverse lunge → halo the other direction → reverse lunge the other leg. Continuous, fluid. The halo loosens the shoulder while the lunge keeps the legs honest.
Figure-8 pass between the legs → step back into a reverse lunge → switch sides. The figure-8 cues hip rotation; the lunge anchors it. Coordination drill as much as conditioning.

sets.notes: Coordination-conditioning hybrids — the upper-body skill challenge slows the leg work down enough that the lunges don't dump the quads. 3 rounds, 30-45s rest between rounds.

sets.name: 🔆 Brutal-Complex Finisher — Light & High-Rep (Rotated In for W15)

exercises.notes:
🔆 **LOAD:** 16-20lb. **Spotlight — the hip-snap:**
- **Hips drive the bell** — it's a hinge that throws the bell out, NOT a squat and NOT an arm-lift
- **Snap the hips to a tall, glute-squeezed lockout**, bell floats to chest height
- **Under fatigue the swing turns into a squat-lift — catch that.** If you feel the knees bending more than the hips hinging, reset the pattern
- Bell to chest height (not overhead), control the backswing
Same bell, goblet position, ab-stance (asymmetric stance), full depth. **SKIP or half the reps if Friday legs cooked the quads** — this is the lever to dial back.
Same bell. Alternating bent-over row — hips hinged, back flat, pull the elbow to the hip. Don't let the back round as the breathing rate climbs.
Bodyweight. Hands at the bell or close together — triceps emphasis. Ribs down, body in one line; drop to the knees if the form breaks late.

sets.notes: **Brutal-complex variant — light bell, higher reps than the Tuesday version.** 3 rounds, continuous within a round, 45-60s rest between rounds. This is conditioning, not a strength finisher — keep moving and keep the breathing rate up. Dial back the squat reps if Friday legs is still in the legs.

exercises.notes: Slow spine wave. Decompress after the high-rep finisher.
60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the lunge flow + cardio-complex squat reps.
60s. Adductors take a hit from the figure-8 + lateral shapes.

tips: **Saturday conditioning option — choice-of-the-day on D6.** Alternates with stairmaster, easy run, or rest. Skip if Friday legs cooked you.
**LIGHT bell throughout: 16-20lb working.** This is the whole point. Conditioning = breathing rate, not load.
**Core blocks carry over:** Asgooch CARDIO complex (row/clean/squat/snatch × 6 × 5 rounds per side) + halo/figure-8-to-reverse-lunge flow combos.
**Finisher rotated to a brutal-complex variant** — light bell, higher reps (swing 15 / ab-stance goblet squat 12 / alternating row 10 each / close-grip pushup 12), 3 rounds.
**Spotlight: the swing hip-snap** — hips drive, not a squat, not an arm-lift. The swing degrades first under fatigue.
**Squatting stays LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Skip/half the goblet-squat reps if the quads are tight.
**Right shoulder watch on the snatch + swing** — sub high pulls if the catch crackles.
**No pull-up greasing here** — Saturday is the conditioning flank.
Rotation plan: W16 swaps the finisher again (100-rep block pull) so Saturday stays fresh.
formPhilosophy: Saturday is conditioning, distinct from the Tue and Thu KB days. Light bell, more reps, more variety. The cave-pull strategy rotates the finisher block week to week — controlled-power, brutal-complex variant, 100-rep blocks — so Saturday builds breadth without going stale or heavy. The day stays explicitly optional: it's the KB flavor of the D6 cardio choice, for days when a treadmill isn't the right call.
